{"answers":[{"answer":"Volunteers stock a €300 pantry (flour, spices, oil). Each session a resident cooks a dish brought by another, using the room’s sink and two portable hotplates. Everyone tastes and writes new contact details on recipe cards. After four weekly cycles, the group publishes a shared cookbook with addresses.","id":"R1"},{"answer":"Volunteers lend six simple digital cameras. Residents photograph meaningful places during the week, return to add sticky-note comments on a wall map. €150 covers printing 50 A5 guides; €150 buys refreshments. After two weeks the group delivers guides door-to-door, exchanging numbers while doing so.","id":"R2"},{"answer":"Six volunteers set two tables in the empty room, label one Swap and one Story. Budget buys tea, biscuits and index cards. Each resident arrives with one item, places it on Swap and speaks for two minutes about its story. Listeners may trade. {"answers":[{"answer":"Session 1: group elects four rotating roles (facilitator, scribe, time-keeper, observer). Each adult secretly writes one concrete sub-skill on a slip. Slips are pooled and randomly paired. Pairs teach each other their sub-skill for ten minutes, scribe records steps on wall chart. Observer notes gaps. Roles rotate after thirty minutes. Session 2: pairs swap partners, teach again, then collectively rehearse full sequence while observer marks checklist items complete. Success visible when all twelve checklist boxes are ticked and every adult can perform the sequence without notes.","id":"R1"},{"answer":"Hour 1: twelve learners form three teams of four. Each team elects facilitator, scribe, time-keeper, observer. Teams list four observable checkpoints on shared poster. Facilitator keeps discussion moving; scribe posts every agreed checkpoint; time-keeper limits talk to fifteen minutes per checkpoint; observer marks live progress. Hour 2: teams rotate members, re-teach checkpoints to new teammates, observer updates poster with green ticks. Success shown when poster displays twelve green ticks and one randomly chosen learner performs full sequence while others confirm each checkpoint aloud.","id":"R2"},{"answer":"Circle drill: learners stand in two concentric rings. Outer member performs one step, inner member immediately repeats it or flags error. After three minutes rings rotate. Every error is taped to wall with correction added by next pair. Hour 2 repeats full sequence while any remaining wall notes must be verbally resolved before next step. Completion when no notes remain and two random members can coach the sequence flawlessly.","id":"R3"}],"memory":{"affect":{"arousal":0.24746275,"disgust":0,"valence":-0.038123585},"associations":[],"content_words":47,"contextual_statements":[{"statement":"I am Claire.","status":"supplied_context_not_acquired_disposition","truncated":false}],"dispositions":[],"episodes":[{"affect":{"arousal":0.6186624,"disgust":0,"valence":-0.69159997},"attribution":"internal","channel":"selfhood","confidence":1,"fidelity":1,"narrative":"For the exhibition I kept responsibility for every decision myself.
